what: The findings this audit made at its first full run, recorded in certs/entropy-arb-audit.json at the commit named, before any fix (the gaps recorded at the pin), with the digests of the modules audited then; each was fixed afterwards in the file named. The audit's declared list (KNOWN in tools/audit-entropy-arb.py) is now empty: any one of these reproducing again fails the run.

findings.name: decide()["H"]
findings.why: fei.decide returns its enclosures as strings cut from str(): ratio [str(r_lo)[:44], str(r_hi)[:44]] and H [str(H_lo)[:30], str(H_hi)[:30]]. Cutting a decimal string rounds toward zero — for a positive upper end, DOWN — so the returned upper end falls below the exact value whenever the cut drops a nonzero digit. The verdict is not affected: decide() compares the full 60-digit r_lo with the threshold, and the full-precision ends (fei.H, fei.ratio) contain the value.
findings.fixedIn: instruments/fei/fei.py: outward(x, digits, up) prints the lower end rounded down and the upper end up (ROUND_FLOOR / ROUND_CEILING) at 43 (ratio) and 29 (H) significant digits

findings.name: decide()["ratio"]

The verdict is not affected: decide() compares the full 60-digit r_lo with the threshold, and the full-precision ends (fei.H, fei.ratio) contain the value.
findings.fixedIn: instruments/fei/fei.py: outward(x, digits, up) prints the lower end rounded down and the upper end up (ROUND_FLOOR / ROUND_CEILING) at 43 (ratio) and 29 (H) significant digits

findings.name: verify_sumdiff.py main(): "ratio in [...]"
findings.why: verify_sumdiff.py and verify_twolaw.py print "ratio in [str(lo)[:44], str(hi)[:44]]": the same cut toward zero, so the printed upper end is below the exact ratio. The verdicts compare the full 120-digit ends; tools/run-optq-ledger.py parses verify_twolaw's printed line into certs/optq-ledger.json.
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_sumdiff.py, tools/verify_twolaw.py: the printed "ratio in [lo, hi]" quantized outward (ROUND_FLOOR for lo, ROUND_CEILING for hi)

findings.name: verify_sumdiff: a non-integer weight that truncates to a law (num 1.9/2 and 1.2/2)
findings.why: read() applies int() to JSON numbers (1.9 -> 1, 1.2 -> 1), so a certificate whose weights are not integers is decided as the law {1/2, 1/2}; sumdiff.js refuses it.
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_sumdiff.py: law() refuses a coordinate or weight that is not an exact integer (a JSON float or a boolean) and a one-point law (every entropy 0, the ratio 0/0); ratio() refuses when the maximum entropy is not separated from 0; each with its reason

findings.name: verify_sumdiff: a boolean weight (true/2)
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_sumdiff.py: law() refuses a coordinate or weight that is not an exact integer (a JSON float or a boolean) and a one-point law (every entropy 0, the ratio 0/0); ratio() refuses when the maximum entropy is not separated from 0; each with its reason

findings.name: verify_sumdiff: a non-integer coordinate (x = 0.5)
findings.why: read() never checks that a coordinate is an integer (the law is taken on R^2); sumdiff.js refuses it.
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_sumdiff.py: law() refuses a coordinate or weight that is not an exact integer (a JSON float or a boolean) and a one-point law (every entropy 0, the ratio 0/0); ratio() refuses when the maximum entropy is not separated from 0; each with its reason

findings.name: verify_sumdiff: a one-point law (p = 1: every entropy 0, the ratio 0/0)
findings.why: every entropy is 0, so the ratio is 0/0; ratio() divides by the max's enclosure [-1E-1000118, 1E-1000118] without checking its sign and returns [-1, -1], and decide() says REFUTED. sumdiff.js refuses it (division by an interval containing 0).
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_sumdiff.py: law() refuses a coordinate or weight that is not an exact integer (a JSON float or a boolean) and a one-point law (every entropy 0, the ratio 0/0); ratio() refuses when the maximum entropy is not separated from 0; each with its reason

findings.name: verify_twolaw: a non-integer weight that truncates to a law (1.9/2 and 1.2/2)
findings.why: laws() applies int() to the weights; twolaw.js refuses it.
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_twolaw.py: decide() refuses a problem field that does not name 3c and two one-point laws (0/0); laws() reads each law through verify_sumdiff's law(), so a non-integer coordinate or weight is refused there; each with its reason

findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_twolaw.py: decide() refuses a problem field that does not name 3c and two one-point laws (0/0); laws() reads each law through verify_sumdiff's law(), so a non-integer coordinate or weight is refused there; each with its reason

findings.name: fei.ln_iv: k = 0 (the docstring's domain is a positive integer)
findings.why: returns (-Infinity, -9.99...E+999999) rather than refusing; unreachable from fei.decide, which calls ln_iv only for a nonzero |a_S|.
